findings.title: God module: supabase.service.ts exceeds 800 LOC with mixed responsibilities
findings.description: The Supabase service file contains 847 lines of code handling authentication, data access, webhook management, and business logic all in a single service. This violates single responsibility principle and makes the module difficult to test and maintain. Multiple unrelated concerns (auth, CRUD operations, webhook handling) are tightly coupled together.

locations.snippet: Service contains: authentication logic, product queries, sales queries, inventory queries, staff management, reconciliation logic, webhook integration, and more

findings.suggested_fix: Split into domain-specific services: AuthService (auth logic), ProductDataService (product CRUD), SalesDataService (sales operations), InventoryDataService (stock management), ReconciliationDataService, and WebhookService (already exists but logic may be duplicated)

findings.title: Missing service layer abstraction: Components directly access Supabase service
findings.description: Multiple page components (sales-dashboard, inventory, products, reconciliation, analysis, staff, owner-dashboard) directly inject and call the monolithic Supabase service. This creates tight coupling between presentation layer and data access, making it difficult to swap implementations, test components in isolation, or refactor data access patterns.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce facade/domain services that wrap Supabase service: SalesService, InventoryService, ProductService (extend existing), ReconciliationService, AnalysisService, StaffService. Components should depend on these domain services, not directly on Supabase.

findings.title: Inconsistent service architecture: ProductService exists but logic may be duplicated in SupabaseService
findings.description: ProductService (149 LOC) exists alongside SupabaseService, but unclear separation of responsibilities. Components may be calling both services or the pattern is inconsistently applied across the codebase. This creates confusion about which service should be used for product operations.

locations.snippet: Also contains product-related queries and mutations

findings.suggested_fix: Establish clear pattern: ProductService should be the only product facade, delegating to SupabaseService for data access. Apply same pattern to other domains (Sales, Inventory, Reconciliation, etc.). Remove duplicate logic from SupabaseService.

findings.title: Sales-management module lacks cohesion with 4 distinct components handling related concerns
findings.description: The sales-management module (800 LOC, 16 files) contains 4 separate components (sales-dashboard, sales-history, sales-lookup, sales-receive) that appear to handle different aspects of sales but lack clear service layer abstraction. Components likely duplicate similar Supabase calls and business logic. No shared sales service layer to coordinate these concerns.
findings.suggested_fix: Create SalesService facade that coordinates sales operations across dashboard, history, and receive functionality. Extract shared queries and mutations to service. Components should use SalesService instead of direct Supabase calls.

findings.title: Layout and UI components tightly coupled with business logic containers
findings.description: Layout components (sidebar, admin-layout, main-layout) are located in src/app/components/ alongside UI components (loading, toast, dashboard-metrics, stock-alerts, activity-feed). Layout containers that manage business state should be separated from pure UI components. Current organization makes it unclear which components handle presentation vs. state management.

locations.snippet: Mixed layout containers and UI components: sidebar (18 LOC), admin-layout (13 LOC), main-layout (36 LOC) alongside dashboard-metrics (29 LOC), stock-alerts (32 LOC), activity-feed (40 LOC)

findings.suggested_fix: Reorganize: Move layout components to src/app/layouts/ or src/app/shell/. Keep src/app/components/ for pure presentational/shared UI components. Consider nesting smart components with their related smart components.

findings.title: Analysis component (292 LOC) has large TypeScript footprint suggesting mixed responsibilities
findings.description: The analysis component contains 292 lines of TypeScript logic alongside 464 lines of HTML and 1128 lines of CSS. This suggests the component may be handling AI report generation logic, data transformation, visualization setup, and presentation—multiple responsibilities that should be separated.

locations.snippet: Large component combining presentation and business logic

findings.suggested_fix: Extract AI report generation and data transformation logic into AnalysisService. Create smaller presentational sub-components for report display sections. Component should only handle view state and delegate to service for calculations and API calls.

findings.title: Authentication logic scattered across multiple locations
findings.description: Auth logic is spread across: auth.guard.ts (37 LOC), login.component.ts (68 LOC), and likely within supabase.service.ts (847 LOC). No centralized AuthService facade exists, making it unclear where authentication state is managed and how to extend auth functionality consistently.

locations.snippet: Auth logic mixed with data access
Auto-logout service with auth session logic

findings.suggested_fix: Create centralized AuthenticationService that consolidates: login/logout logic, session management, token refresh, and auth state. Auth guard and login component should use AuthenticationService exclusively. Move auth-related logic from SupabaseService to AuthenticationService.

findings.title: Webhook and notification services lack clear abstraction boundaries
findings.description: WebhookService (40 LOC), ToastService (32 LOC), and notification-related logic may be scattered. Unclear how external webhooks, internal notifications, and user-facing toasts coordinate. Potential for duplicate notification handling logic.
findings.suggested_fix: Establish clear notification flow: External events → WebhookService → internal domain events → ToastService (for UI feedback). Document when each service should be used. Consider creating NotificationCoordinatorService if cross-cutting logic exists.

findings.title: Cross-cutting concerns (Loading, AutoLogout, PageReload) lack centralized orchestration
findings.description: Three utility services manage application-wide concerns: LoadingService (26 LOC), AutoLogoutService (74 LOC), PageReloadService (71 LOC). These services likely have complex interdependencies and subscribe to shared state but lack orchestration. No clear owner for managing their lifecycle and interactions.
findings.suggested_fix: Create AppStateService or StateOrchestrationService that manages loading, session, and page state as cohesive unit. These utilities should not directly manage global state independently but coordinate through central service.

findings.title: Missing repository pattern for data persistence abstraction
findings.description: All data access goes directly through SupabaseService without repository pattern. No abstraction layer between business logic (components/services) and Supabase SDK. If database provider needs to change (e.g., from Supabase to Firebase), all components and services require modification.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement Repository pattern with typed repositories for each domain entity: ProductRepository, SalesRepository, InventoryRepository, etc. These should abstract Supabase SDK and expose domain-specific methods. Facilitates testing with mock repositories and easier migration to different backends.

coupling_assessment: High coupling between components and data access layer. Most page components directly depend on the monolithic SupabaseService (god module). Presentation layer is tightly coupled to Supabase SDK implementation details. Missing domain service facades creates cascading changes when business logic needs modification. Cross-cutting concerns (loading, auth, notifications) are scattered across multiple services without clear coordination.
layering_assessment: Incomplete layering structure. Current layers: Components → SupabaseService → Supabase SDK. Missing: (1) Domain/Business Service layer for coordinating business rules, (2) Repository pattern for data persistence abstraction, (3) API/DTO layer for request/response transformation, (4) State management coordination. Layout components and business container components are not clearly separated. Auth logic is scattered across guard, component, and service instead of centralized in auth service.
summary: The codebase has 9 significant structural issues primarily stemming from a god module (SupabaseService at 847 LOC) and absence of domain service facades. Components bypass business logic layer and access data directly, creating tight coupling. Sales management (800 LOC, 4 components) lacks cohesive service. Authentication concerns are scattered across 4 locations without centralized abstraction. Missing repository pattern makes database provider changes expensive. Layout/UI component organization is unclear. Cross-cutting services (loading, logout, reload) lack orchestration. While the Angular 19 framework conventions are followed, the application lacks proper architectural layering—it needs domain services, repository pattern, centralized auth service, and separation of concerns to improve from 52 (significant structural problems) toward 70+ (good structure).
